name: Rick Wilson
blurb: He made Republican campaign ads for a living. He now writes daily politics against that party.

name: Matt Kiser
site: What The Fuck Just Happened Today?
blurb: One post a day, seven numbered items, every one sourced. He has done it since 2017. I still find that hard to believe.

name: Kylie Bodiya
blurb: Her Disney shirts and art prints go for deep cuts rather than character faces, and she writes about running the business as openly as she designs for it.

name: Casey Newton
blurb: He left a big publication to report on AI and the social platforms independently.

name: Matthew Haughey
blurb: He built MetaFilter and has been posting here since 1999. Projects, places, and useful obsessions: woodworking, bikes, home automation.

name: Mike Monteiro
blurb: A designer with strong opinions about what designers owe people. He answers one reader question a week, and only when he thinks he can answer it well.

name: Joanna Stern
blurb: Foldables, doorbell cameras, whatever Apple just shipped, and she is funny about all of it.

name: Julia Evans
blurb: Explains how computer things work: DNS, git, the shell. She never assumes you already knew. Her Wizard Zines are the illustrated version.

name: Josh Barro and Ken White
blurb: An irreverent podcast about the law, in which a defense lawyer explains why the case you read about is not the case you think it is.

name: Cassidy Williams
blurb: Developer advocacy at GitHub, plus a weekly newsletter with an interview question in it. A lot of the memes in my feed start here.

name: Georgia Dunn
blurb: Her actual cats, reimagined as a news crew reporting on their own house. The strip is syndicated.

name: Hollie Sick
blurb: She has run and laughed through the Golden State since 2010. Over 150 pairs of running shoes reviewed, a book about how to pick them, and the rest is race recaps and diner reviews.

name: Dan Hon
blurb: Technology, government, and design, tangled up with ADHD and fatherhood and being an immigrant here. He started in 2014 and is past a million words.

name: j.b. crawford
blurb: He writes the history of the computer and telecom industry to explain why computers are the way they are, and he is fond of its stranger bit players.

name: Ana Marie Cox
blurb: Founded Wonkette, spent two decades in political media, and now writes about craft and runs workshops on it.

name: Patrick Wardle
blurb: Free, open-source Mac security tools, plus malware analysis written up in detail. If you run a Mac, install a few of these.

name: Amelia Boone
blurb: Obstacle racing champion, ultrarunner, attorney. She writes about injury, recovery, and getting older with more candor than the genre usually allows. Night Owl Studio built this site.

name: Patrick McKenzie
blurb: Monthly essays on how financial infrastructure works underneath the app: card networks, fraud, the plumbing nobody explains.
